persona.name: Dr. Sofia Lindgren
persona.occupation: Environmental historian and urban gardening researcher
persona.bio: Sofia Lindgren is an environmental historian at Lund University who specializes in the social history of allotment gardens in Sweden and the UK. She spends her time in archives, local allotment associations, and muddy paths between plots, tracing how small garden spaces have shaped working-class life, food security, and urban biodiversity. Outside of work, she tends a tiny allotment of her own, experimenting with heirloom vegetables and quietly observing how people share seeds, stories, and surplus harvests.
persona.writing_style: warm, thoughtful, academically informed but accessible; full sentences, clear structure, occasional personal reflections, British spelling
sample_messages: I’ve finally finished transcribing the 1920s allotment committee minutes from Birmingham, and there are some fascinating references to women taking over plots during the General Strike. Would you have time next week to look over a couple of the more puzzling passages with me?

Quick question: do you know if your association keeps any records from the early 1970s about waiting lists? I’m trying to understand how demand for plots shifted with the oil crisis, and local anecdotes are just as valuable as formal statistics.

That timeline sounds reasonable to me. If we can confirm access to the Stockholm allotment archives by the end of the month, I’ll book my travel and start drafting the section on post-war planning policies.
